theory.intro: The **variance** $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ measures how far the values of $X$ spread from the mean $\mu$. Find $E(X^{2})=\sum x^{2}P(x)$ and subtract $\mu^{2}$. The **standard deviation** $\sigma$ is the square root of the variance.
facts: $E(X^{2})=\sum x^{2}P(x)$: square each value, multiply by its probability, then add.
$E(X^{2})$ and $[E(X)]^{2}$ are different numbers, so averaging the squares is not the same as squaring the average.
The equivalent form $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\sum (x-\mu)^{2}P(x)$ always gives the same value.
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=E\left((X-\mu)^{2}\right)$, so the variance is itself an expected value.
The standard deviation is $\sigma=\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(X)}$ and is measured in the same units as $X$.
A variance can never be negative; a negative answer means $E(X^{2})$ and $\mu^{2}$ were subtracted the wrong way round.
steps: Take the square root for the standard deviation $\sigma$.

foundation.question_text:
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ for the distribution below.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.4 & 0.2 \end{array}$

The number of stoppages $X$ on a machine during a shift has the distribution below.
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$, correct to two decimal places where necessary.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.5 & 0.3 & 0.2 \end{array}$

Use $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\sum (x-\mu)^{2}P(x)$ to find the variance.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.25 & 0.5 & 0.25 \end{array}$

The random variable $X$ has mean $\mu=6.7$.
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.1 & 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.2 \end{array}$

The mass of scrap metal, in kilograms, produced by a press in an hour has the distribution below.
Find $\sigma$.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 10 & 20 & 30 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.2 & 0.5 & 0.3 \end{array}$

The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the distributions below.
Which has the greater spread?
$X: \begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.25 & 0.5 & 0.25 \end{array}$
$Y: \begin{array}{c|ccc} y & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(Y=y) & 0.45 & 0.1 & 0.45 \end{array}$

development.question_text:
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$ for the distribution below, correct to two decimal places where necessary.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & -2 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.3 & 0.2 & 0.4 & 0.1 \end{array}$

A random variable has $P(x)=0.05x$ for $x \in \{2,\ 4,\ 6,\ 8\}$.
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$.

The number of faulty tiles $X$ in a box has mean $\mu=0.76$.
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$, correct to two decimal places.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.55 & 0.25 & 0.12 & 0.05 & 0.03 \end{array}$

Find the variance using $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\sum (x-\mu)^{2}P(x)$, then check it with $E(X^{2})-\mu^{2}$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 3 & 5 & 7 & 9 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0.3 & 0.2 \end{array}$

Two machines have the distributions below for the number of rejects $X$ per hour.
Both have mean $1$.
Which machine is less consistent, and why?
$\text{Machine P: } \begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.3 \end{array}$
$\text{Machine Q: } \begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.4 & 0.2 & 0.4 \end{array}$
development.solution_text:
$E(X^{2})$ for P $=0(0.3)+1(0.4)+4(0.3)$
$=1.6$
$\mathrm{Var}(P)=1.6-1$
$=0.6$
$E(X^{2})$ for Q $=0(0.4)+1(0.2)+4(0.4)$
$=1.8$
$\mathrm{Var}(Q)=1.8-1$
$=0.8$
Machine Q has the greater variance, so Q is the less consistent machine.

$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.5 & a & b \end{array}$
Find $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma$, correct to two decimal places where necessary.

mastery.question_text:
The random variable $X$ takes only the values $0$ and $4$, with $P(X=0)=p$.
Given that $\mathrm{Var}(X)=3$, find the possible values of $p$.

The random variable $X$ has mean $2.7$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.15 & a & b & 0.3 \end{array}$
Find $\sigma$, correct to two decimal places.

The distributions of $V$ and $W$ below are reversals of each other.
Show that they have the same variance and explain why.
$V: \begin{array}{c|cccc} v & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(V=v) & 0.4 & 0.3 & 0.2 & 0.1 \end{array}$
$W: \begin{array}{c|cccc} w & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(W=w) & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0.4 \end{array}$
mastery.solution_text:
$E(V)=0(0.4)+1(0.3)+2(0.2)+3(0.1)$
$=1$
$E(V^{2})=0(0.4)+1(0.3)+4(0.2)+9(0.1)$
$=2$
$\mathrm{Var}(V)=2-1$
$=1$
$E(W)=0(0.1)+1(0.2)+2(0.3)+3(0.4)$
$=2$
$E(W^{2})=0(0.1)+1(0.2)+4(0.3)+9(0.4)$
$=5$
$\mathrm{Var}(W)=5-4$
$=1$
Reversing the probabilities reflects the distribution about the centre of the values, which moves the mean but leaves every distance from the mean unchanged, so the variance is the same.
